==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃ep-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|official}}, from {{der|en|fro|official}}, from {{der|en|la|officiālis}}, from {{der|en|la|officium||duty, service}}, {{surf|en|office|-ial|nocap=1}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈfɪʃ.əl/|[əˈfɪʃ.əɫ]|[əˈfɪʃ.ɫ̩]|a=UK,US,CA,AU}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-official.ogg|a=California}}
* {{IPA|en|/əˈfəʃ.əl/|[əˈfəʃ.ɫ̩]|[əˈfəʃ.ʊ]|a=NZ}}
* {{hyph|en|of|fi|cial}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪʃəl|s=3}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# Of or about an office or [[public trust]].
#: {{ux|en|'''official''' duties}}
# Derived from the proper office or officer, or the appropriate authority; made or communicated by authority
#: {{ux|en|an '''official''' statement or report}}
# Approved by authority; [[authorized]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''Official''' Strategy Guide}}
## (Of a statement) [[dubious|Dubious]] but recognized by authorities as the [[truth]] or [[canon]].
##: {{ux|en|Despite these testimonies, "accidental asphyxiation" remains his '''official''' cause of death.}}
# {{lb|en|pharmacology}} Sanctioned by the [[pharmacopoeia]]; appointed to be used in medicine; [[officinal]].
#: {{ux|en|an '''official''' drug or preparation}}
# Discharging an office or function.
#* {{RQ:Browne Pseudodoxia Epidemica|edition=2nd|passage=the stomach and other parts '''official''' unto nutrition}}
# Relating to an office, especially a subordinate executive officer or attendant.
# Relating to an ecclesiastical judge appointed by a bishop, chapter, archdeacon, etc., with charge of the spiritual jurisdiction.
# {{lb|en|informal}} [[true|True]], [[real]], beyond [[doubt]].
#: {{ux|en|Well, it's '''official''': you lost your mind!}}
# {{lb|en|pharmacology}} Listed in a national [[pharmacopeia]].

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# An [[office holder]], a [[person]] [[hold]]ing an [[#Adjective|official]] [[position]] in [[government]], [[sports]], or [[other]] [[organization]].<!--not limited to government-->
#: {{ux|en|'''Officials''' in the Firefly administration assure the Sylvanians they don't want war either.}}
#: {{ux|en|In most soccer games, there are three '''officials''': the referee and two linesmen.}}
#: {{ux|en|The company's '''officials''' became [[nabob]]s as it took on more and more power after [[Plassey]].}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1941|author=w:George Orwell|title={{w|The Lion and the Unicorn: Socialism and the English Genius|The Lion and the Unicorn}}|section=Pt. III
|passage=...'''officials''' with their [[prehensile]] bottoms...}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2014-03-15|volume=410|issue=8878
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21598997-american-regulators-should-block-comcasts-proposed-deal-time-warner-cable-turn-it Turn it off]
|passage=If the takeover is approved, Comcast would control 20 of the top 25 cable markets […] Antitrust '''officials''' will need to consider Comcast’s status as a [[monopsony]] (a buyer with disproportionate power), when it comes to negotiations with programmers, whose channels it pays to carry.}}
